characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: Rigaku D/Max-2200 X-ray diffractometer, Cu target operated at 40 kV and 40 mA, graphite monochromator, wavelength λ = 0.154056 nm
characterization_methods.key_findings: The as-cast strips mainly consist of austenite and ferrite with an ordered DO3 phase; a double peak between 43.5° and 45.0° is (110)δ and (220)DO3; the (110)δ/(220)DO3 area ratio decreases with increasing Cr content, indicating Cr promotes the δ-ferrite → DO3 transformation.
characterization_methods.purpose: Phase identification of the as-cast (and annealed) steel strips

characterization_methods.key_findings: The irregularly shaped δ-ferrite is distributed in the γ-austenite matrix; the as-cast 6Cr strip has a δ-ferrite volume fraction of 18%; Cr addition changes short rod-shaped ferrite into block ferrite.
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: after mechanical polishing and etching (3.3 vol% nitric acid, 3.3 vol% acetic acid, 0.1 vol% hydrofluoric acid; etching time 3 s); photographs taken at 0.5 mm from the strip surface along the thickness direction
characterization_methods.purpose: Characterize the microstructure and measure the δ-ferrite volume fraction

characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: JEOL-2010F TEM operated at 200 kV; specimens prepared by twin-jet electrolytic polishing at −30 °C and 30 V with 10% perchloric acid + 90% alcohol
characterization_methods.key_findings: In the as-cast 6Cr strip the κ-carbide superlattice reflection is barely visible (very small volume fraction); the measured lattice parameter of κ-carbides and γ-austenite is 0.389 nm and 0.384 nm respectively; DO3 phase with size 28 ± 4 nm precipitates in the δ-ferrite (no significant change vs 3Cr).
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: BF images, DF images using (001)/(00-2) superlattice reflections, SADP along [110] zone axis
characterization_methods.purpose: Elucidate the nano-scale precipitated phases in γ-austenite and δ-ferrite
characterization_methods.technique: Transmission Electron Microscopy (TEM) with selected area diffraction (SADP) and dark-field (DF) imaging

characterization_methods.key_findings: As-cast 6Cr: YS 718 ± 17 MPa, UTS 1001 ± 3 MPa, TE 38 ± 4 % (Table 2).
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: constant strain rate 2.5×10^-4 s^-1, per GB/T-228.1-2010; specimens with gage width 4 mm and gage length 12 mm machined from the steel strips; tested at least 3 times
characterization_methods.purpose: Measure the mechanical (tensile) properties of the as-cast and annealed strips
characterization_methods.technique: Uniaxial tensile testing at room temperature

characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: AccuPyc II 1340 Gas Displacement Density Analyzer
characterization_methods.key_findings: Measured average density of the 6Cr steel strip is 6.66 g/cm^3.
characterization_methods.purpose: Measure the average density of the steel strips

characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: Inductively Coupled Plasma Mass Spectrometry (ICP) and CS2800 carbon-sulfur analyzer
characterization_methods.key_findings: Measured composition of the 6Cr steel strip (wt.%): Mn 20.18, Al 9.12, C 1.20, Cr 6.08, S 0.0011, Fe Bal. (Table 1).
characterization_methods.purpose: Measure the compositions of the steel strips

interfaces.interface_notes: The irregularly shaped δ-ferrite insets in γ-austenite; DO3 ordered phase occupies the δ-ferrite whereas κ-carbides precipitate in the γ-austenite.
interfaces.phase_evolution: In the as-cast strips the XRD shows a double peak between 43.5° and 45.0° corresponding to (110)δ and (220)DO3; the area ratio of the (110)δ peak to the (220)DO3 peak gradually decreases with increasing Cr content, indicating that Cr promotes the transformation from δ-ferrite to the ordered DO3 phase.

comparative_performance.comparison_metric: Yield strength of the as-cast 6Cr strip (718 ± 17 MPa) is lower than that of the as-cast Cr-free (0Cr) strip (836 ± 7 MPa), while UTS and total elongation do not change obviously; the highest UTS × TE product (38.0 GPa %) is achieved in the as-cast 6Cr steel strip.

processing_steps.method: centrifugal casting under near-rapid solidification (near-net shape strip casting)
processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: A 100 g alloy ingot was prepared by cold-crucible levitation melting of 99.99% pure iron, 99.9% pure manganese, 99.9% pure aluminum, 99.9% pure chromium and 99.8% high-purity graphite; the ingot was remelted by induction melting and the molten metal was poured into a copper mold rotating at 600 rpm. The as-cast steel strips had size 80 mm × 60 mm × 2.5 mm. This is the as-cast state of the 6Cr strip.

measurement_conditions.other_conditions: tensile tests performed at least 3 times on a MTS Criterion 44 Mechanical Property Tester
measurement_conditions.specimen_geometry: gage width 4 mm, gage length 12 mm

measurement_conditions.other_conditions: measured by an AccuPyc II 1340 Gas Displacement Density Analyzer

phases_present.morphology: matrix; BF image shows a featureless dark band/matrix region

precipitates.distribution: nano-scale particles within γ-austenite; the volume fraction is very small in the as-cast 6Cr strip (the [110] SADP superlattice reflection intensity is barely visible)

microstructure_list.region: γ-austenite matrix (SEM photographs taken at 0.5 mm from strip surface along thickness direction)

phases_present.crystal_structure: bcc (ferrite); ordered DO3 phase with space group Fm3m, lattice parameter a = 0.565 nm
phases_present.morphology: irregularly shaped, coarse block-like ferrite; the short rod-shape ferrite of low-Cr strips changes into block ferrite with Cr addition

precipitates.distribution: densely distributed DO3 nano-particles in the δ-ferrite (DF image using (00-2) superlattice reflection)

microstructure_list.region: δ-ferrite particles distributed in γ-austenite matrix

structures.overall_structure: As-cast near-rapidly solidified 6Cr strip consists mainly of γ-austenite matrix with irregular δ-ferrite evenly distributed in it; nano-scale κ-carbides are present in the γ-austenite and an ordered DO3 phase is present in the δ-ferrite. Cr addition increases the volume fraction and size of δ-ferrite and promotes the δ-ferrite → ordered DO3 transformation.

unmapped_findings: The product of ultimate tensile strength and total elongation (UTS × TE) of the as-cast 6Cr steel strip is 38.0 GPa %, the highest among all the studied strips (Table 2).
Measured lattice parameter of the κ-carbides and γ-austenite in the as-cast 6Cr steel strip is 0.389 nm and 0.384 nm, respectively.

The yield strength of the as-cast 6Cr steel strip (718 MPa) is higher than that of the as-cast 3Cr steel strip (642 MPa), attributed to solid solution strengthening caused by the higher Cr content, because precipitation strengthening is low in both as-cast 3Cr and 6Cr strips due to the small κ-carbide volume fraction.

The strain hardening rate of the two as-cast Cr-containing steel strips (including 6Cr) gradually decreases during deformation; the 'hump' present in the strain hardening rate curve of the Cr-free steel becomes weak with Cr addition.
The DO3 phase size in the as-cast 6Cr strip (28 ± 4 nm) shows no significant change compared with the as-cast 3Cr strip (30 ± 3 nm).
Nominal composition of the alloy is Fe-20Mn-9Al-1.2C-6Cr (wt. %); measured composition (Table 1): Mn 20.18, Al 9.12, C 1.20, Cr 6.08, S 0.0011, Fe Bal. (wt. %).
